facts.text: Topock was originally called Mellen, a railroad station and steamboat landing where the Atlantic and Pacific Railroad built the Red Rock Bridge in 1890 after earlier bridges failed.
The town’s name comes from Captain Jack Mellon, a 40‑year veteran steamboat captain, misspelled as “Mellen” when the station was named.
Topock Marina sits just off I‑40 on Historic Route 66, serving as a traditional refueling point for boaters between Needles and Lake Havasu City.
In 1930, PG&E completed a 40,000‑mile natural gas pipeline from Texas to San Francisco, placing a compressor station at Topock on the Colorado River.
The 1930s PG&E compressor station used hexavalent chromium for rust prevention, leading to environmental concerns that prompted cleanup under RCRA and CERCLA.
